text:
The fix is verified. Tracing through the test cases:

1. **`wrap("the quick brown fox", 10)`**: "the quick" (9 chars) + "brown" would be 15 > 10 → new line; "brown fox" (9) → `["the quick", "brown fox"]` ✓
2. **`wrap("aaa bbb", 7)`**: 3+1+3 = 7 ≤ 7 → stays on one line → `["aaa bbb"]` ✓ (this was the reported bug)
3. **`wrap("aaa bbb ccc", 7)`**: "aaa bbb" fills exactly 7, "ccc" (11 > 7) wraps → `["aaa bbb", "ccc"]` ✓
4. **`wrap("abcdefghij", 4)`**: long-word splitting path is untouched → `["abcd", "efgh", "ij"]` ✓

The one-character fix (`<` → `<=`) makes the code match its documented behavior: a line may be exactly `width` characters long.
